# `modules/EditorMeshOps.js`

> **Source:** `editor/js/modules/EditorMeshOps.js`

============================================================================ EditorMeshOps.js — Mesh operations for editor entities  Exposes Kaolin mesh ops (subdivide, smooth, normals, validate, flip) on selected entities. Each op clones the mesh, runs the Kaolin function, re-registers with CustomMeshRegistry + EntityMeshRenderer, and pushes an undo snapshot (hybrid: auto for <50k tris, confirm dialog for larger). ============================================================================

## Functions

### `getMeshDataForEntity(editor, entityId)`

Get mesh geometry data for an entity. Checks CustomMeshRegistry first, then EntityMeshRenderer cache.

**Parameters:**

- `editor` *(Object)* — EditorApp instance
- `entityId` *(number)* — _No description in source JSDoc._

**Returns:** | null}

### `async applyMeshOp(editor, entityId, opName, params = {})`

Apply a mesh operation to an entity. Pipeline: get mesh → optional undo snapshot → run op → re-register → update entity.

**Parameters:**

- `editor` *(Object)* — EditorApp instance
- `entityId` *(number)* — Target entity
- `opName` *(string)* — Operation identifier
- `params` *(Object)* — Operation-specific parameters

**Returns:** true if operation succeeded

## Notes & Examples

### Editor Extension System

The editor supports extensions via the same Plauna component system as apps. Extensions can add panels, tools, menu items, and hooks into the engine. They run with elevated 'editor' capability granting access to the scene graph, asset database, and build pipeline.

**Example: Editor extension adding a custom panel**
```js
import { Extension } from 'editor/core/Extension.js';
import { Panel } from 'editor/ui/Panel.js';

class TerrainEditor extends Extension {
  id = 'terrain-editor';
  capabilities = ['editor', 'scene'];
  
  activate(context) {
    // Add menu item
    context.menus.add('Tools/Terrain', () => this.open());
    
    // Register tool
    context.tools.register('terrain', {
      icon: 'mountain',
      onSelect: (entity) => this.edit(entity)
    });
  }
  
  open() {
    this.panel = new Panel({
      title: 'Terrain Editor',
      content: this.buildUI()
    });
    context.workspace.addPanel(this.panel);
  }
  
  edit(entity) {
    const terrain = entity.get(TerrainComponent);
    this.panel.bind(terrain);
  }
}

editor.extensions.register(TerrainEditor);
```
